summary: Mrs. Hidary explores the reunion between Yaakov and Esav in Parashat Vayishlah, focusing on Yaakov's fear and his strategic preparations. She compares the relationship between Yaakov and Esav to the story of Kayin and Hevel, while highlighting how Esav's character has evolved over twenty years. The class also discusses Yaakov's wrestling match at the Yabok, where he receives the name Yisrael, and connects these themes to the resilience of the Jewish people in the face of modern-day challenges.
questions: Why does the Torah repeat the word 'brother' so many times in the story of Yaakov and Esav?
Is Esav the same person he was twenty years ago?
What does it mean that Yaakov is called Yisrael?
How should we interpret the reunion between Yaakov and Esav?
What can we learn from Yaakov's fear and his preparations for meeting Esav?
